memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: God also said to Abraham, "As for Sarai your wife, you are no longer to call her Sarai; her name will be Sarah. I will bless her and will surely give you a son by her. I will bless her so that she will be the mother of nations; kings of peoples will come from her." - Gen 17:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
It is not only Abraham who receives a new name - Sarai becomes Sarah, "princess," and God speaks a lavish blessing over her: "I will bless her... she will be the mother of nations; kings of peoples will come from her." Notice how personal and specific this is. Sarah, the barren wife who had waited decades in disappointment, is named and blessed directly by God.

This matters. In her culture, a barren woman was often overlooked, even pitied or shamed. But God does not overlook Sarah. He names her, blesses her, and places her at the very centre of His covenant purposes. The one the world might have written off becomes the mother of nations and kings.

See how God repeats "I will bless her" - twice in one breath. God delights to lavish blessing on those who have known long disappointment. Sarah's decades of waiting were not forgotten; they were the prelude to an outpouring of grace.

There is such encouragement here for anyone who has waited long and felt overlooked. God sees you, names you, and has blessing in store that His delays could never cancel. Sarah is later honoured among the heroes of faith (Heb 11:11), the once-barren woman through whom the promise flowed. The God who so blessed Sarah has not forgotten you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you felt overlooked in a long season of disappointment?
- Do you believe God still has blessing in store for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You see and name those the world overlooks. Like Sarah, I have known waiting and disappointment. Help me trust that Your delays cannot cancel Your blessing. You have not forgotten me.
Amen.
